chief_complaint: Obesity with prediabetes and stage‑1 hypertension, complicated by psychosocial stressors (intimate partner violence, social isolation).
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 52‑year‑old woman with long‑standing obesity (BMI ≥30 since 1997) and prediabetes (A1c 6.1% documented since 1987). Blood pressure measured most recently at 132/84 mmHg meets criteria for stage‑1 hypertension, yet no antihypertensive therapy is recorded. She has no active prescription medications. Psychosocial stressors have escalated over the past few years: chronic stress noted from 2017, social isolation and part‑time employment beginning in 2019, and intimate‑partner abuse identified in early 2020. Preventive care includes a colon polyp removed in April 2020 and routine dental care. Overall healthcare utilization has been low (23 visits over 33 years) with limited follow‑up after 2020. Several key laboratory and lifestyle data (lipids, renal function, smoking, alcohol use, physical activity) are missing, hindering full risk assessment.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include gingivitis and primary dental caries (treated 2019‑2020), a colon polyp removed in April 2020, acute bronchitis and associated acetaminophen use in 2017, multiple lacerations in 2017, knee injury and patellar tendon rupture resolved in 2016, prior stress finding resolved in 2017, and a transition from full‑time to part‑time employment in 2019.
social_determinants: Intimate partner violence, social isolation, part‑time employment (potential financial strain), low healthcare utilization, limited preventive follow‑up, and possible lack of health insurance coverage.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure: 132/84 mmHg (stage‑1 hypertension). A1c: 6.1% (prediabetic). BMI data missing but obesity documented. No lipid panel, eGFR, or smoking/alcohol information available. Charlson comorbidity index = 0; clinical complexity rated moderate. Combined metabolic (obesity, prediabetes, hypertension) and psychosocial (abuse, isolation, stress) risk places the patient at elevated cardiovascular, renal, and mental‑health risk.

clinical_impression: Middle‑aged woman with significant metabolic risk (obesity, prediabetes, stage‑1 hypertension) that is currently untreated, compounded by severe psychosocial stressors including intimate‑partner violence and social isolation. Data gaps in key laboratory values, lifestyle factors, and mental‑health assessment limit precise risk stratification, but overall risk for cardiovascular disease, progression to diabetes, renal impairment, and mental‑health disorders is high.
